description: New-onset type 2 diabetes: first T2DM diagnosis, with no T2DM diagnosis in the 365 days before it, and at least 365 days of continuous observation_period coverage before the diagnosis.
sql:
WITH t2dm AS (
    SELECT co.person_id, co.condition_start_date
    FROM omop.condition_occurrence co
    WHERE co.condition_source_value = '44054006' -- SNOMED: type 2 diabetes mellitus
),
first_dx AS (
    SELECT t.person_id, MIN(t.condition_start_date) AS dx_date
    FROM t2dm t
    GROUP BY t.person_id
)
SELECT
    p.person_id,
    fd.dx_date AS index_date,
    EXTRACT(YEAR FROM fd.dx_date) - p.year_of_birth AS age_at_dx,
    CASE p.gender_concept_id WHEN 8507 THEN 'Male' WHEN 8532 THEN 'Female' END AS sex
FROM first_dx fd
JOIN omop.person p ON p.person_id = fd.person_id
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM t2dm prior
        WHERE prior.person_id = fd.person_id
          AND prior.condition_start_date < fd.dx_date
          AND prior.condition_start_date >= fd.dx_date - INTERVAL '365 days'
    )
  AND EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM omop.observation_period op
        WHERE op.person_id = fd.person_id
          AND op.observation_period_start_date <= fd.dx_date - INTERVAL '365 days'
          AND op.observation_period_end_date >= fd.dx_date
    )
-- Load-bearing: a stable order keeps the LIMIT picking the same persons at every re-run.
ORDER BY p.person_id
LIMIT 5000
explanation: One row per person. The index date is the person's earliest condition_occurrence with SNOMED source code 44054006 (type 2 diabetes mellitus). The query applies two filters. First, a NOT EXISTS check removes anyone with another T2DM record in the 365 days before the index date. Because the index date is already the first diagnosis, this check never removes anyone; it is kept to state the washout criterion explicitly. Second, an EXISTS check requires a single observation_period that starts at least 365 days before the index date and is still running on that date, which gives at least one year of continuous prior coverage. The output columns are person_id, the index date, age at diagnosis (diagnosis year minus year of birth) and sex. No vocabulary tables are used.
assumptions: T2DM is identified only by condition_source_value = '44054006' (SNOMED, as Synthea emits it). Trusts that record ICD-10 (E11.x) or other local codes in condition_source_value will need those codes added.
The standard concept for T2DM (201826) is not in FLIP's safe concept list, so the query does not filter on condition_concept_id.
'Continuous coverage' means one observation_period row that spans the whole 365 days up to and including the diagnosis date. Adjacent periods are not merged.
'First diagnosis' means first recorded in this trust's data. The 365-day prior-observation requirement is what supports calling it new-onset.
This is not an imaging cohort, so no accession_id is projected.
LIMIT 5000 is an arbitrary cap. Raise it if the trust cohort is larger.

description: Adults aged 40-80 with incident atrial fibrillation. Exclude anyone with a prior stroke, anyone with a mechanical heart valve, and anyone who died within 30 days of the AF diagnosis.
sql: WITH af_events AS (SELECT co.person_id, co.condition_start_date FROM omop.condition_occurrence co WHERE co.condition_source_value IN ('49436004', '282825002', '440059007', '440028005') OR co.condition_source_value LIKE 'I48%'), first_af AS (SELECT ae.person_id, MIN(ae.condition_start_date) AS af_date FROM af_events ae GROUP BY ae.person_id), incident_af AS (SELECT fa.person_id, fa.af_date FROM first_af fa WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM omop.observation_period op WHERE op.person_id = fa.person_id AND op.observation_period_start_date <= fa.af_date - INTERVAL '365 day' AND op.observation_period_end_date >= fa.af_date)) SELECT p.person_id, ia.af_date AS af_diagnosis_date, EXTRACT(YEAR FROM ia.af_date) - p.year_of_birth AS age_at_af, CASE p.gender_concept_id WHEN 8507 THEN 'Male' WHEN 8532 THEN 'Female' END AS sex FROM omop.person p JOIN incident_af ia ON ia.person_id = p.person_id WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM ia.af_date) - p.year_of_birth BETWEEN 40 AND 80 AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM omop.condition_occurrence s WHERE s.person_id = p.person_id AND s.condition_start_date <= ia.af_date AND (s.condition_source_value IN ('230690007', '422504002', '432504007', '274100004') OR s.condition_source_value LIKE 'I61%' OR s.condition_source_value LIKE 'I63%' OR s.condition_source_value LIKE 'I64%')) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM omop.condition_occurrence v WHERE v.person_id = p.person_id AND (v.condition_source_value = '429064006' OR v.condition_source_value LIKE 'Z95.2%' OR v.condition_source_value LIKE 'Z952%')) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM omop.observation ov WHERE ov.person_id = p.person_id AND (ov.observation_source_value = '429064006' OR ov.observation_source_value LIKE 'Z95.2%' OR ov.observation_source_value LIKE 'Z952%')) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM omop.death d WHERE d.person_id = p.person_id AND d.death_date <= ia.af_date + INTERVAL '30 day') ORDER BY p.person_id LIMIT 5000
explanation: Vocabulary-free tabular cohort, one row per person. The index date is the first atrial fibrillation record, matched on condition_source_value. The SNOMED AF codes are matched exactly and ICD-10 I48.x by prefix. A diagnosis counts as incident only if the person had at least 365 days of observation before it, so earlier AF is unlikely to be missed. Age at diagnosis is EXTRACT(YEAR FROM af_date) - year_of_birth and must be 40-80 inclusive. Exclusions: (1) any stroke recorded on or before the AF date (SNOMED codes, or ICD-10 I61/I63/I64); (2) a mechanical or prosthetic heart valve recorded at any time, in condition_occurrence or observation; (3) a death date within 30 days after the AF date. The output gives person_id, AF diagnosis date, age at AF and sex. No free text or identifiers are returned. It ends with ORDER BY person_id LIMIT 5000 so the cohort is stable across re-runs.
assumptions: This is a tabular (non-imaging) cohort, so accession_id is not projected.
Synthea-style SNOMED codes, or ICD-10 codes on UK trusts, are assumed to be held in condition_source_value and observation_source_value.
'Incident' is taken to mean the first AF record with at least 365 days of prior observation. Trusts with no observation_period rows will return an empty cohort; drop that EXISTS clause if so.
'Prior stroke' includes a stroke recorded on the same day as the AF diagnosis (<=), to be conservative.

A mechanical heart valve excludes the person regardless of when it was recorded. ICD-10 Z95.2 covers any prosthetic heart valve, not only mechanical ones, so this exclusion may be slightly broader than requested.
I am not certain that SNOMED 429064006 means mechanical/prosthetic heart valve presence; please verify it. Valve-replacement procedures in procedure_occurrence are not checked.
I am not fully certain that SNOMED 432504007 (cerebral infarction) and 274100004 (cerebral haemorrhage) are correct; please verify them.
The 30-day death exclusion uses death_date <= af_date + 30 days. Persons with no death record are kept.
concepts_used: 429064006 = Presence of prosthetic/mechanical heart valve (SNOMED, uncertain)
Z95.2 / Z952 = Presence of prosthetic heart valve (ICD-10)

description: Patients newly diagnosed with hypertension who started an ACE inhibitor (lisinopril, ramipril or enalapril) within 90 days after the diagnosis.
sql: WITH first_dx AS (SELECT co.person_id, MIN(co.condition_start_date) AS dx_date FROM omop.condition_occurrence co WHERE co.condition_source_value = '38341003' OR co.condition_concept_id = 320128 GROUP BY co.person_id), ace_exposures AS (SELECT de.person_id, de.drug_exposure_start_date AS start_date FROM omop.drug_exposure de WHERE de.drug_concept_id IN (1308216, 1334456, 1341927) OR de.drug_source_value IN ('29046', '314076', '35296', '3827') UNION ALL SELECT dr.person_id, CAST(dr.drug_era_start_date AS DATE) AS start_date FROM omop.drug_era dr WHERE dr.drug_concept_id IN (1308216, 1334456, 1341927)), first_ace AS (SELECT ae.person_id, MIN(ae.start_date) AS first_ace_date FROM ace_exposures ae GROUP BY ae.person_id) SELECT p.person_id, fd.dx_date AS hypertension_dx_date, fa.first_ace_date AS ace_inhibitor_start_date, fa.first_ace_date - fd.dx_date AS days_dx_to_ace, EXTRACT(YEAR FROM fd.dx_date) - p.year_of_birth AS age_at_dx, CASE WHEN p.gender_concept_id = 8532 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_female FROM omop.person p JOIN first_dx fd ON fd.person_id = p.person_id JOIN first_ace fa ON fa.person_id = p.person_id WHERE fa.first_ace_date >= fd.dx_date AND fa.first_ace_date <= fd.dx_date + INTERVAL '90 days' AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM omop.observation_period op WHERE op.person_id = p.person_id AND op.observation_period_start_date <= fd.dx_date - INTERVAL '365 days' AND op.observation_period_end_date >= fd.dx_date) ORDER BY p.person_id LIMIT 5000
explanation: Vocabulary-free cohort, one row per person. 'Newly diagnosed' means the person's earliest hypertension record is the index date, and the person must have at least 365 days of observation before it, so earlier unrecorded diagnoses are less likely. Hypertension is matched on the SNOMED source code 38341003 or the standard concept 320128. ACE-inhibitor exposures for lisinopril, ramipril or enalapril come from two places: drug_exposure (ingredient concept ids or RxNorm source codes) and drug_era (where drug_concept_id is ingredient-level by OMOP convention). The person's first-ever ACE-inhibitor start must fall on or within 90 days after the index date. Because it is the first ever, people already taking an ACE inhibitor before diagnosis are excluded, which matches 'started'. Output columns are diagnosis date, ACE start date, days between them, age at diagnosis and sex. Rows are ordered by person_id with a literal LIMIT so the cohort is the same each time the query is re-run.
assumptions: Concept ids 1308216 (lisinopril), 1334456 (ramipril) and 1341927 (enalapril) are the standard RxNorm ingredient concepts as I recall them. They are not in FLIP's guaranteed list, so please verify them against the trust's data.

drug_exposure.drug_concept_id usually holds clinical-drug-level concepts, not ingredients. Matching it on ingredient ids therefore only catches ingredient-level records. drug_era (ingredient level) and drug_source_value RxNorm codes are used to cover the rest. If drug_era is not populated at a trust, matching relies on source values.

The RxNorm source codes are not certain. 29046, 35296 and 3827 are believed to be the ingredient RxCUIs for lisinopril, ramipril and enalapril. 314076 is lisinopril 10 MG Oral Tablet, which Synthea emits. Other ramipril or enalapril product-level RxCUIs used by Synthea or by trust feeds may be missed and should be added locally.

Hypertension is matched on SNOMED 38341003 (as in the Synthea tutorial) or standard concept 320128 (essential hypertension). Descendant codes such as secondary hypertension are not included because concept_ancestor is not used.
'Newly diagnosed' requires the first hypertension record plus at least 365 days of prior observation. Trusts with short or missing observation_period data will return fewer patients.
The 90-day window is inclusive: ACE start on day 0 through day 90 after diagnosis.
concepts_used: 314076 = RxNorm RxCUI: lisinopril 10 MG Oral Tablet (drug_source_value)

description: Chronic kidney disease by lab: eGFR below 60 on at least 2 occasions at least 90 days apart. Only use eGFR results recorded in mL/min/1.73m2.
sql:
WITH egfr_low AS (
    -- eGFR results below 60, restricted to results reported in mL/min/1.73m2
    SELECT
        m.person_id,
        m.measurement_date,
        m.value_as_number
    FROM
        omop.measurement m
    WHERE
        m.measurement_source_value IN (
            '33914-3',  -- eGFR MDRD
            '48642-3',  -- eGFR MDRD, non-Black
            '48643-1',  -- eGFR MDRD, Black
            '50044-7',  -- eGFR MDRD, female
            '62238-1',  -- eGFR CKD-EPI
            '69405-9',  -- eGFR (unspecified method)
            '77147-7',  -- eGFR MDRD (alternate)
            '88293-6',  -- eGFR CKD-EPI, Black
            '88294-4',  -- eGFR CKD-EPI, non-Black
            '98979-8'   -- eGFR CKD-EPI 2021
        )
        AND LOWER(m.unit_source_value) IN (
            'ml/min/1.73m2',
            'ml/min/{1.73_m2}',
            'ml/min/1.73 m2',
            'ml/min/1.73m^2',
            'ml/min/1.73 m^2'
        )
        AND m.value_as_number IS NOT NULL
        AND m.value_as_number < 60
),
ckd AS (
    -- persons whose earliest and latest low eGFR are at least 90 days apart,
    -- i.e. at least two low results separated by >= 90 days
    SELECT
        el.person_id,
        MIN(el.measurement_date) AS first_low_egfr_date,
        MAX(el.measurement_date) AS last_low_egfr_date,
        COUNT(*) AS n_low_egfr_results,
        MIN(el.value_as_number) AS min_egfr
    FROM
        egfr_low el
    GROUP BY
        el.person_id
    HAVING
        MAX(el.measurement_date) >= MIN(el.measurement_date) + INTERVAL '90 days'
)
SELECT
    p.person_id,
    EXTRACT(YEAR FROM c.first_low_egfr_date) - p.year_of_birth AS age_at_first_low_egfr,
    CASE p.gender_concept_id WHEN 8507 THEN 'Male' WHEN 8532 THEN 'Female' END AS sex,
    c.first_low_egfr_date,
    c.last_low_egfr_date,
    c.n_low_egfr_results,
    c.min_egfr
FROM
    omop.person p
    JOIN ckd c ON c.person_id = p.person_id
-- Load-bearing: a stable order keeps the LIMIT picking the same persons at every re-run.
ORDER BY
    p.person_id
LIMIT 5000
explanation: Vocabulary-free cohort of persons with lab-defined chronic kidney disease. eGFR results are identified by LOINC codes in measurement_source_value and kept only when value_as_number < 60 and the unit_source_value (case-insensitively) is one of the common spellings of mL/min/1.73m2. A person qualifies when their earliest and latest low eGFR results are at least 90 days apart, which is equivalent to having at least two low results separated by >= 90 days. One row per person with age at first low eGFR, sex, first/last low eGFR dates, the number of low results and the lowest eGFR value. Ordered by person_id with a literal LIMIT for stability.
assumptions: eGFR is identified via LOINC codes in measurement_source_value (Synthea emits 33914-3); trusts that store local lab codes there instead will need their codes added. Some of the listed LOINC codes (e.g. 77147-7, 50044-7, 69405-9) are from memory and should be verified.

The unit filter matches unit_source_value text variants of mL/min/1.73m2 (including UCUM 'mL/min/{1.73_m2}'); results with a missing or differently spelled unit are excluded, per the request to only use results recorded in mL/min/1.73m2. unit_concept_id was not used because no unit concept id is in the safe list.
The 'at least 2 occasions at least 90 days apart' criterion is implemented as max(low date) >= min(low date) + 90 days, with no requirement that intervening results also be low.
Results reported with an operator (e.g. '<60') are taken at their numeric value; values like '>60' with value_as_number = 60 are not counted as below 60.
Sex is shown only for gender concept ids 8507/8532; other values appear as NULL.

description: Patients who had a colonoscopy and then a CT of the abdomen within 30 days after it, one row per CT study.
sql: WITH colonoscopy AS (SELECT po.person_id, po.procedure_date FROM omop.procedure_occurrence po WHERE po.procedure_source_value = '73761001' OR po.procedure_concept_id = 4249893), abdo_ct AS (SELECT io.image_occurrence_id, io.person_id, io.accession_id, io.image_study_uid, io.image_occurrence_date FROM omop.image_occurrence io JOIN omop.procedure_occurrence ctp ON ctp.procedure_occurrence_id = io.procedure_occurrence_id WHERE io.modality_concept_id = 4300757 AND ctp.procedure_source_value = '169070004'), ct_study AS (SELECT MIN(ac.image_occurrence_id) AS image_occurrence_id FROM abdo_ct ac GROUP BY ac.person_id, COALESCE(ac.image_study_uid, ac.accession_id, CAST(ac.image_occurrence_id AS varchar))) SELECT ac.person_id, ac.accession_id, ac.image_occurrence_id, ac.image_occurrence_date AS ct_date, MAX(c.procedure_date) AS last_colonoscopy_date, ac.image_occurrence_date - MAX(c.procedure_date) AS days_after_colonoscopy, EXTRACT(YEAR FROM ac.image_occurrence_date) - p.year_of_birth AS age_at_ct, CASE p.gender_concept_id WHEN 8507 THEN 'Male' WHEN 8532 THEN 'Female' END AS sex FROM ct_study cs JOIN abdo_ct ac ON ac.image_occurrence_id = cs.image_occurrence_id JOIN omop.person p ON p.person_id = ac.person_id JOIN colonoscopy c ON c.person_id = ac.person_id AND c.procedure_date <= ac.image_occurrence_date AND c.procedure_date >= ac.image_occurrence_date - INTERVAL '30 days' GROUP BY ac.image_occurrence_id, ac.person_id, ac.accession_id, ac.image_occurrence_date, p.year_of_birth, p.gender_concept_id ORDER BY ac.image_occurrence_id LIMIT 1000
explanation: Vocabulary-free cohort of abdominal CT studies that follow a colonoscopy within 30 days. Colonoscopies come from procedure_occurrence, matched on the SNOMED source code 73761001 or the standard concept id 4249893. CT studies are image_occurrence rows with modality 4300757 (CT). Each must be linked through procedure_occurrence_id to a procedure whose source code is 169070004 (CT of abdomen). Multiple series of the same study are collapsed to one row per study, keeping the lowest image_occurrence_id per image_study_uid, falling back to accession_id. Each study is kept only if the same person had a colonoscopy on or up to 30 days before the CT date. The most recent qualifying colonoscopy date, days elapsed, age at CT and sex are returned as features. Ordered by image_occurrence_id with a literal LIMIT for stable re-runs.
assumptions: The safe concept list has no abdominal anatomic_site_concept_id, so 'CT of the abdomen' is identified through the linked procedure_occurrence source code 169070004. CT rows with no linked procedure_occurrence_id, or coded differently (e.g. a combined abdomen/pelvis CT code), are excluded. Trusts may need to add their local codes or an abdominal anatomic_site_concept_id.

SNOMED 73761001 (Colonoscopy) is the code Synthea emits. OMOP concept id 4249893 is believed to be the standard 'Colonoscopy' concept but should be verified locally. Other colonoscopy variants (e.g. with biopsy or polypectomy) are not included.
I am fairly but not fully certain that SNOMED 169070004 means 'CT of abdomen'; please verify.
'Within 30 days after' is read as a CT dated on the same day as the colonoscopy or up to 30 days later. Same-day CTs are included because dates alone cannot show which came first.
'One row per CT study' collapses series sharing an image_study_uid (or accession_id if the UID is missing). The returned image_occurrence_id and accession_id belong to the representative row.
LIMIT 1000 is an arbitrary cap; adjust as needed.

description: For each patient, the first ever pneumonia diagnosis (use a window function), with age at that diagnosis and how many pneumonia diagnoses they had in total.
sql:
WITH pneumonia AS (
    SELECT
        co.condition_occurrence_id,
        co.person_id,
        co.condition_start_date,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY co.person_id
            ORDER BY co.condition_start_date, co.condition_occurrence_id
        ) AS rn,
        COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY co.person_id) AS n_pneumonia_diagnoses
    FROM
        omop.condition_occurrence co
    WHERE
        co.condition_source_value = '233604007' -- SNOMED: pneumonia (disorder)
)
SELECT
    p.person_id,
    pn.condition_occurrence_id AS first_pneumonia_condition_occurrence_id,
    pn.condition_start_date AS first_pneumonia_date,
    EXTRACT(YEAR FROM pn.condition_start_date) - p.year_of_birth AS age_at_first_pneumonia,
    CASE p.gender_concept_id WHEN 8507 THEN 'Male' WHEN 8532 THEN 'Female' END AS sex,
    pn.n_pneumonia_diagnoses
FROM
    pneumonia pn
    JOIN omop.person p ON p.person_id = pn.person_id
WHERE
    pn.rn = 1
ORDER BY
    p.person_id
LIMIT 5000
explanation: Vocabulary-free cohort with one row per patient who has at least one pneumonia diagnosis. The CTE takes every pneumonia row from condition_occurrence, matched on condition_source_value. It uses two window functions: ROW_NUMBER() ranks each patient's diagnoses by start date, with condition_occurrence_id as a tie-breaker so the result is deterministic. COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY person_id) gives the patient's total number of pneumonia diagnoses. The outer query keeps only the first-ranked row and joins to person to compute age at that diagnosis as EXTRACT(YEAR FROM diagnosis date) - year_of_birth, plus sex. It ends with ORDER BY person_id (the primary key) and a literal LIMIT so the cohort stays stable across approval and training. This is not an imaging cohort, so accession_id is not needed.
assumptions: Pneumonia is identified only by condition_source_value = '233604007' (the SNOMED code for pneumonia, as emitted by Synthea). Subtypes coded differently are not included, such as viral or bacterial pneumonia under other SNOMED codes. Trusts that only populate condition_concept_id (e.g. standard concept 255848) would need that added. I am fairly but not fully certain this single code covers the local coding.
The total pneumonia count is the number of condition_occurrence rows with that code. Repeated recordings of the same episode are each counted.
Age is approximated from the calendar year only (year of diagnosis minus year_of_birth), as the rules require, so it may be off by one.
LIMIT 5000 is an arbitrary cap on cohort size; adjust it if more patients are needed.
concepts_used: 233604007 = SNOMED CT pneumonia (disorder), matched on condition_source_value

description: Patients admitted as inpatients with a primary heart failure diagnosis recorded during the inpatient stay, with the length of stay of that admission.
sql: WITH hf_admission AS (SELECT vo.visit_occurrence_id FROM omop.visit_occurrence vo WHERE vo.visit_concept_id IN (9201, 262) AND vo.visit_end_date IS NOT NULL AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM omop.condition_occurrence co WHERE co.person_id = vo.person_id AND co.condition_status_concept_id = 32902 AND (co.condition_source_value IN ('84114007', '42343007', '88805009', '85232009', '703272007', '446221000') OR co.condition_source_value LIKE 'I50%') AND (co.visit_occurrence_id = vo.visit_occurrence_id OR (co.condition_start_date >= vo.visit_start_date AND co.condition_start_date <= vo.visit_end_date)))) SELECT vo.person_id, vo.visit_occurrence_id, vo.visit_concept_id, vo.visit_start_date AS admission_date, vo.visit_end_date AS discharge_date, (vo.visit_end_date - vo.visit_start_date) AS length_of_stay_days, EXTRACT(YEAR FROM vo.visit_start_date) - p.year_of_birth AS age_at_admission, CASE p.gender_concept_id WHEN 8507 THEN 'Male' WHEN 8532 THEN 'Female' END AS sex FROM omop.visit_occurrence vo JOIN hf_admission ha ON ha.visit_occurrence_id = vo.visit_occurrence_id JOIN omop.person p ON p.person_id = vo.person_id ORDER BY vo.visit_occurrence_id LIMIT 5000
explanation: One row per inpatient admission (visit_concept_id 9201 inpatient or 262 ER-and-inpatient) that has a heart-failure condition flagged as the primary diagnosis and recorded during that stay. The condition must either be linked to the admission through visit_occurrence_id or start between the admission and discharge dates. Heart failure is matched on condition_source_value using SNOMED codes (as Synthea emits them) and ICD-10 I50.x codes (as NHS trusts typically record them), so no vocabulary tables are needed. Length of stay is the discharge date minus the admission date, in days. Age at admission and sex are included as clinical features. The query ends with ORDER BY on the visit primary key and a literal LIMIT so the cohort is the same each time it is re-run.
assumptions: 'Primary diagnosis' is taken as condition_status_concept_id = 32902 (OMOP Condition Status 'Primary diagnosis'). This id is not in FLIP's list of known concept ids. Trusts that do not populate condition_status_concept_id, including Synthea-derived data, will return no rows. Drop that predicate if every recorded heart-failure diagnosis during the stay should count.

The heart-failure SNOMED codes (84114007, 42343007, 88805009, 85232009, 703272007, 446221000) are believed correct, but the list may not be exhaustive. Trusts recording ICD-10 source values are covered by LIKE 'I50%'. Other local coding schemes would be missed.
Inpatient admissions are visit_concept_id 9201 and 262. Admissions with no visit_end_date are excluded because their length of stay cannot be computed.
Length of stay is in whole days (visit_end_date - visit_start_date), so a same-day discharge counts as 0.
A person may appear once per qualifying admission. person_id is exposed so the trust can count distinct subjects.
This is not an imaging cohort, so accession_id is not included.

description: Patients with a continuous metformin drug era of at least 180 days, using drug_era, with their condition_era count for type 2 diabetes.
sql: WITH metformin_eras AS (SELECT de.person_id, COUNT(*) AS n_metformin_eras_180d, MIN(de.drug_era_start_date) AS first_long_era_start, EXTRACT(DAY FROM MAX(de.drug_era_end_date - de.drug_era_start_date)) AS longest_metformin_era_days FROM omop.drug_era de WHERE de.drug_concept_id = 1503297 AND de.drug_era_end_date >= de.drug_era_start_date + INTERVAL '180 days' GROUP BY de.person_id), t2dm_eras AS (SELECT ce.person_id, COUNT(*) AS n_t2dm_condition_eras, SUM(ce.condition_occurrence_count) AS n_t2dm_occurrences_in_eras FROM omop.condition_era ce WHERE ce.condition_concept_id = 201826 GROUP BY ce.person_id) SELECT p.person_id, CASE WHEN p.gender_concept_id = 8532 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_female, EXTRACT(YEAR FROM me.first_long_era_start) - p.year_of_birth AS age_at_first_long_metformin_era, me.n_metformin_eras_180d, me.longest_metformin_era_days, COALESCE(te.n_t2dm_condition_eras, 0) AS n_t2dm_condition_eras, COALESCE(te.n_t2dm_occurrences_in_eras, 0) AS n_t2dm_occurrences_in_eras FROM omop.person p JOIN metformin_eras me ON me.person_id = p.person_id LEFT JOIN t2dm_eras te ON te.person_id = p.person_id ORDER BY p.person_id LIMIT 5000

For each person the query returns the number of such eras, the length in days of the longest one, and age at the start of the first one. It also returns sex and the number of type 2 diabetes condition_era rows plus the summed condition_occurrence_count across those eras. The diabetes counts come through a LEFT JOIN with COALESCE to 0, so metformin users with no T2DM era are kept and get a count of 0. drug_era and condition_era have no *_source_value columns, so the filters use standard concept ids directly; omop.concept is not needed. 'Continuous' is taken to mean a single drug_era row, which already merges exposures separated by up to the trust's persistence window (gap_days). An era counts if its duration is at least 180 days.

Tabular cohort with no imaging, so accession_id is not exposed.
